name: christianpure-natural-events
title: Earthquakes, eclipses and famines in the Bible, set against the scientific record
description: Every natural event the Bible and two early church writers name (earthquakes, eclipses and darkness, famines and droughts), each matched to earthquake catalogues, eclipse canons and climate records and given one of four grades, with the nearest fault, how common such events were, and every source. Rows with no match stay in.

sources.title: NOAA NCEI/WDS Global Significant Earthquake Database (public domain), doi:10.7289/V5TD9V7K
NOAA NCEI/WDS Global Historical Tsunami Database (public domain), doi:10.7289/V5PN93H7
CFTI5Med, Catalogue of Strong Earthquakes in Italy and the Mediterranean, Guidoboni et al. 2018/2019 (CC BY 4.0), via PANGAEA
GEM Global Active Faults Database, Styron and Pagani 2020 (CC BY-SA 4.0)
Five Millennium Canon of Solar Eclipses and of Lunar Eclipses, Espenak and Meeus (NASA)
JPL DE441 ephemeris (Park et al. 2021), via Skyfield
Christian Pure Bible places (CC BY 4.0), built on OpenBible.info and Pleiades

resources.name: natural-events
resources.title: Events and grades
resources.description: One row per natural event named in the Bible or early church writings, with its place, the passage's date, the grade and the best match in the scientific record.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Short id of the event. Starts with e- (eclipse or darkness), f- (famine or drought) or q- (earthquake).

fields.name: kind
fields.description: earthquake, eclipse, darkness, famine or drought.

fields.name: event
fields.description: Short title of the event.

fields.name: passages
fields.description: Where the event is told: Bible references, or the ancient writer for the two rows outside the Bible.

fields.name: place
fields.description: The place used for matching: where the passage puts the event, or the nearest place it names.

fields.name: place_id
fields.description: Id of the place in the Christian Pure Bible places list, or add-… for the two places added here (see place-additions.csv).

fields.name: latitude
fields.description: WGS 84 latitude of the place.

fields.name: longitude
fields.description: WGS 84 longitude of the place.

fields.name: passage_date_from
fields.description: Earliest year scholars give for the passage. Negative years are BC: -760 is 760 BC (there is no year 0).

fields.name: passage_date_to
fields.description: Latest year scholars give for the passage, same numbering.

fields.name: passage_date
fields.description: The same range in words, for example 766 BC to 751 BC.

fields.name: date_note
fields.description: Where the date range comes from and where scholars disagree.

fields.name: grade
fields.description: One of four: strong match, possible match, no match found, beyond the records. See the README for what each means.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Why the row has its grade, naming the record it rests on.

fields.name: best_match
fields.description: The record that comes closest. Empty where nothing comes close; starts with None. where the nearest candidate does not fit.

fields.name: best_match_catalogue
fields.description: The catalogue or writer that holds the best match.

fields.name: best_match_entry
fields.description: The entry's number in that catalogue, where it has one.

fields.name: best_match_year
fields.description: Year of the best match, same numbering as passage_date_from.

fields.name: how_common
fields.description: How often events of this kind happened at this place in the same period, counted from the same records (earthquakes within 200 km; eclipses visible from the place).

fields.name: nearest_fault_km
fields.description: Earthquake rows: distance in km from the place to the nearest mapped active fault (GEM Global Active Faults).

fields.name: nearest_fault
fields.description: Earthquake rows: that fault's type and slip rate. Most faults in this region have no name in the source.

fields.name: nearest_fault_gem_id
fields.description: Earthquake rows: the fault's id in the GEM file (catalogue name and id).

fields.name: graded_on
fields.description: Date the grade was last set, YYYY-MM-DD.

resources.name: natural-events-sources
resources.title: Sources
resources.description: Every source consulted for each event, numbered as in the research notes.

fields.name: event_id
fields.description: Event (natural-events.csv).

fields.name: n
fields.description: Number of the source within its event.

fields.name: citation
fields.description: The citation, with a note where the source was not opened or is cited only to show a claim exists.

fields.name: url
fields.description: Link or DOI for the source, where there is one.

resources.name: earthquake-candidates
resources.title: Earthquake candidates
resources.description: Every catalogue earthquake within 200 km of an earthquake row's place and within 25 years either side of its date range. An event with no candidates has one row with the catalogue fields empty.

fields.name: event_id
fields.description: Event (natural-events.csv).

fields.name: catalogue
fields.description: NOAA NCEI significant earthquakes, NOAA NCEI tsunamis, or CFTI5Med.

fields.name: entry
fields.description: Entry number in that catalogue. CFTI5Med notes in brackets: N = no observations behind the entry, S = a single data point, D = doubtful.

fields.name: year
fields.description: Year the catalogue gives, same numbering as natural-events.csv.

fields.name: where
fields.description: Place name the catalogue gives.

fields.name: size
fields.description: Magnitude (M, Mw) or intensity (I0) where the catalogue gives one.

fields.name: distance_km
fields.description: Distance in km from the event's place to the catalogue's epicentre.

fields.name: catalogue_flag
fields.description: Where the catalogue itself marks the entry as doubtful or as resting on no observations.

fields.name: base_count_100y
fields.description: Catalogue earthquakes within 200 km in the 50 years either side of the middle of the passage's range.

fields.name: base_rate_per_century
fields.description: Catalogue earthquakes within 200 km per century, 2150 BC to AD 500.

resources.name: eclipse-visibility
resources.title: Eclipse visibility
resources.description: What each proposed eclipse looked like from Jerusalem, Samaria and Nineveh, from the Christian Pure sky engine (JPL DE441), worked out three times: at the engine's central value for the slowing of Earth's spin (Delta T) and at two standard errors either side.

fields.name: event
fields.description: Event (natural-events.csv).

fields.name: kind
fields.description: solar or lunar.

fields.name: nasa_catalogue_number
fields.description: Number of the same eclipse in NASA's Five Millennium Canon, for reference.

fields.name: date_julian
fields.description: Date (Universal Time) in the Julian calendar, astronomical year first: -762 Jun 15 is 15 June 763 BC.

fields.name: nasa_type
fields.description: NASA's type for the eclipse as a whole: T total, A annular, H hybrid, P partial.

fields.name: local_type
fields.description: The eclipse as seen from the place at the central Delta T: Total, Annular or Partial (lunar: the eclipse's own type).

fields.name: delta_t_case
fields.description: central, minus_2sigma or plus_2sigma.

fields.name: delta_t_s
fields.description: Delta T used, in seconds.

fields.name: delta_t_2sigma_s
fields.description: Two standard errors of Delta T, in seconds (Morrison and Stephenson 2004, 0.8 t^2 s; stretched before 1000 BC).

fields.name: place_id
fields.description: Place id.

fields.name: place
fields.description: Jerusalem, Samaria or Nineveh.

fields.name: visible
fields.description: yes or no. Solar: the sun was up while partly covered. Lunar: the moon was up during the shadow (umbral) phase. Normal bending of light at the horizon is counted.

fields.name: magnitude
fields.description: Solar: fraction of the sun's width covered at greatest eclipse at the place. Lunar: umbral magnitude.

fields.name: altitude_deg
fields.description: Height of the sun (solar) or moon (lunar) above the horizon at greatest eclipse, degrees. Negative means below the horizon.

fields.name: minutes_visible
fields.description: Minutes the eclipse (solar) or its umbral phase (lunar) could be seen with the sun or moon up.

fields.name: local_start
fields.description: Central Delta T only: local mean time the eclipse (solar) or umbral phase (lunar) began, HH:MM.

fields.name: local_greatest
fields.description: Central Delta T only: local mean time of greatest eclipse, HH:MM.

fields.name: local_end
fields.description: Central Delta T only: local mean time the eclipse or umbral phase ended, HH:MM.

fields.name: ut_greatest
fields.description: Central Delta T only: Universal Time of greatest eclipse, HH:MM.

fields.name: first_seen_local
fields.description: Central Delta T only: local mean time the eclipse could first be seen, HH:MM.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Warnings, for example where the Delta T error formula is used outside its stated range.

resources.name: eclipse-counts
resources.title: Eclipse counts
resources.description: For each eclipse or darkness row, every eclipse in the sky engine's table inside the passage's date range that was visible from the row's place at the central Delta T: how common eclipses were.

fields.name: event_id
fields.description: Event (natural-events.csv).

fields.name: place
fields.description: Place the eclipses were worked out for.

fields.name: range
fields.description: The passage's date range.

fields.name: kind_counted
fields.description: What was counted: solar eclipses covering half the sun or more at greatest eclipse with the sun up, or lunar eclipses with the moon up during the shadow (umbral) phase.

fields.name: visible_count
fields.description: How many eclipses were counted.

fields.name: per_century
fields.description: visible_count per hundred years.

fields.name: visible_list
fields.description: The counted eclipses, separated by "; ": date (Julian calendar) and fraction of the sun covered, or minutes of the lunar shadow phase with the moon up.

resources.name: grade-log
resources.title: Grade changes
resources.description: Every change to a grade after first release, with its date and reason. Empty until a grade changes.

fields.name: event_id
fields.description: Event (natural-events.csv).

fields.name: date
fields.description: Date of the change, YYYY-MM-DD.

fields.name: old_grade
fields.description: Grade before.

fields.name: new_grade
fields.description: Grade after.

fields.name: why
fields.description: What changed: a new study, a corrected figure, or a reviewer's reading.
